meta.title: One agent payment, first step to last

views.label: The call
views.note: The agent calls the wallet. The wallet's own delegated code answers, in the wallet's own storage.

views.label: Resolving the policy
views.note: Three hops, inside the transaction. No CCIP-read gateway, because ENSv2 resolve() returns data directly.

views.label: Judgement
views.note: The account decides whether to trust the policy. The policy decides whether the spend is allowed.

views.label: Effect
views.note: A block emits an event and returns normally, so the agent can read the refusal on its next tick.

segments.label: Resolve the policy through ENS — on every payment, inside the transaction
Effect, and what the agent can see next

messages.label: spend(token, payee, amount)
messages.note: Is the caller a bound agent, not revoked, and is the account unpaused? Reasons 1, 2 and 10 stop here.

messages.label: write the ledger, then transfer — only on 0
SpendExecuted — or SpendBlocked, and no money moved
the agent reads this on its next tick

cards.title: What is actually running
items: The wallet is a plain EOA delegated under EIP-7702 to the LeashAccount implementation
So this code executes in the wallet’s own storage, at the wallet’s own address — msg.sender for the transfer is the wallet
The agent is only a msg.sender that a policy recognises: it holds no funds and no permissions

cards.title: Where each refusal comes from
items: 1 AGENT_NOT_BOUND · 2 AGENT_REVOKED · 3 NO_POLICY · 4 POLICY_NOT_APPROVED · 10 PAUSED · 12 POLICY_FAILED — all decided by LeashAccount
5 TOKEN_NOT_ALLOWED · 6 PAYEE_NOT_ALLOWED · 7 OVER_TX_LIMIT · 8 OVER_PERIOD_LIMIT · 9 OUTSIDE_TIME_WINDOW · 11 OVER_SHARED_LIMIT — all decided by the policy
The numbers are frozen: the subgraph, the frontend and the agent all depend on them

cards.title: A block does not revert
items: It emits SpendBlocked and returns normally, so the subgraph can index the refusal
The cost is that a successful receipt is not a successful payment
12 POLICY_FAILED is deliberately not 4 — "this policy is broken" and "no human approved this" have different fixes

cards.title: Why the walk cannot wedge the account
items: resolvePolicy never reverts: a failed hop is reason 3 and no money moves
No externally returned data reaches abi.decode — every hop reads its words in assembly and checks structure and padding itself
The three hops return 32, 32 and 96 bytes; hop three returns bytes, so offset and length come first
